'''Merlise Aycock Clyde''' is an American statistician known for her work in [[ensemble learning|model averaging]] for [[Bayesian statistics]]. She is a professor of Statistical Science and immediate past chair of the Department of Statistical Science at [[Duke University]].{{r|profile}} She was president of the [[International Society for Bayesian Analysis]] (ISBA) in 2013,{{r|isba}} 
and chair of the Section on Bayesian Statistical Science of the [[American Statistical Association]] for 2018.{{r|sbss}}

==Education==
Clyde graduated from [[Oregon State University]] in 1985 with a [[Bachelor of Science]] in Forestry. She earned two master's degrees, one from the [[University of Alberta]] in 1986 in Forest Biometrics and another from the [[University of California, Riverside]] in 1988 in Statistics, before completing her Ph.D. at the [[University of Minnesota]] in 1993 in Statistics.{{r|profile}} Her dissertation, supervised by [[Kathryn Chaloner]], was ''Bayesian Optimal Designs for Approximate Normality''{{r|mgp}}, which received the Savage Award for outstanding dissertation in Bayesian econometrics and statistics in 1994.{{r|savage}}

==Awards and honors==
Clyde is a [[fellow of the American Statistical Association]], of the [[International Society for Bayesian Analysis]],{{r|profile}} and of the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]].{{r|ims}} She was one of two winners of the Zellner Medal of the ISBA in 2016 "for their outstanding service to ISBA".{{r|zellner}}
